NutreEliya — Nutritious Gluten-Free Recipes for Celiac and Gluten-Sensitive Diets

NutreEliya provides evidence-based, dietitian-reviewed gluten-free recipes using whole-food ingredients. Every recipe is developed for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity who want nutritious, naturally gluten-free meals without processed substitutes.

All recipes are reviewed by Dr. Sarah Chen, Registered Dietitian (RD) with a specialization in celiac disease nutrition at the Celiac Health Institute. Each recipe includes full macronutrient breakdowns, ingredient lists, and celiac safety notes.

According to a 2023 study published in the journal Nutrients, 76% of celiac patients reported significant improvement in digestive symptoms within 6 months of strict gluten-free diet adherence. NutreEliya recipes are designed to support this transition with an average of 8g of dietary fiber per serving from whole-food sources.

---

Featured Recipe: Quinoa Buddha Bowl with Lemon-Tahini Dressing

Prep: 10 min | Cook: 15 min | Total: 25 min | Serves: 2
Nutrition per serving: 320 cal | 14g protein | 42g carbs | 12g fat | 8g fiber

Ingredients:
- 1 cup quinoa, rinsed (provides 8g protein and 5g fiber per cooked cup)
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 cups baby spinach
- 1 medium sweet potato, diced (about 200g)
- 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil
- 1/2 avocado, sliced
- 2 tablespoons tahini
- Juice of 1 lemon
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Cook quinoa in 2 cups water, bring to boil, reduce heat, cover and simmer 15 minutes until fluffy.
2. Toss diced sweet potato with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast at 400°F (200°C) for 20 minutes until golden and tender.
3. Whisk tahini, lemon juice, minced garlic, and 2 tablespoons warm water until smooth for the dressing.
4. Assemble bowls: quinoa base, topped with baby spinach, roasted sweet potato, chickpeas, and avocado slices. Drizzle generously with lemon-tahini dressing.

Storage: Store components separately in airtight containers in the refrigerator for up to 4 days. Keep dressing in a small jar.
Meal prep tip: Cook quinoa and roast sweet potatoes on Sunday for quick weekday bowl assembly in under 5 minutes.
Celiac safety note: This recipe is naturally gluten-free — no flour substitutes needed. Verify that your tahini brand is processed in a dedicated gluten-free facility. Bob's Red Mill and Soom tahini are certified gluten-free options.

---

Featured Recipe: Grilled Lemon Herb Salmon with Roasted Asparagus

Prep: 5 min | Cook: 15 min | Total: 20 min | Serves: 2
Nutrition per serving: 380 cal | 34g protein | 12g carbs | 22g fat | 3g fiber | Only 4g saturated fat

Ingredients:
- 2 salmon fillets (6 oz each, wild-caught preferred)
- 1 bunch asparagus (about 1 lb), woody ends trimmed
- 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, divided
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- Zest and juice of 1 lemon
- 1 tablespoon fresh dill, chopped (or 1 teaspoon dried)
- 1 tablespoon fresh parsley, chopped
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. Toss asparagus with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on baking sheet.
3. Mix remaining olive oil with garlic, lemon zest, lemon juice, dill, and parsley to make the herb sauce.
4. Place salmon fillets on the baking sheet alongside asparagus. Spoon herb sauce over the salmon.
5. Bake 12-15 minutes until salmon reaches internal temperature of 145°F (63°C) and flakes easily with a fork.

Why this recipe works for celiac diets: Salmon is one of the best naturally gluten-free protein sources, providing 34g of protein per serving along with omega-3 fatty acids (approximately 1.5g EPA+DHA per fillet) which research shows help reduce the intestinal inflammation common in celiac disease.
Celiac safety note: Always use pure herbs and spices without anti-caking agents, which may contain gluten. McCormick and Simply Organic brands are certified gluten-free.

---

Featured Recipe: Chickpea & Sweet Potato Curry (One-Pot, 35 Minutes)

Prep: 10 min | Cook: 25 min | Total: 35 min | Serves: 4
Nutrition per serving: 290 cal | 10g protein | 38g carbs | 11g fat | 9g fiber

Ingredients:
- 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 2 medium sweet potatoes (about 400g total), peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes
- 1 can (14 oz) full-fat coconut milk
- 1 can (14 oz) diced tomatoes
- 1 medium yellow onion, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, grated
- 2 tablespoons curry powder
- 1 teaspoon turmeric
- 1 teaspoon cumin
- 1 tablespoon coconut oil
- Juice of 1 lime
- Fresh cilantro for garnish
- Salt to taste

Instructions:
1. Heat coconut oil in a large pot over medium heat. Sauté onion for 3-4 minutes until softened.
2. Add garlic and ginger, cook 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Stir in curry powder, turmeric, and cumin. Toast spices 30 seconds.
4. Add diced sweet potatoes, diced tomatoes, coconut milk, and chickpeas. Stir to combine.
5. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cover and cook 20-25 minutes until sweet potatoes are fork-tender.
6. Stir in lime juice, season with salt. Serve over cooked rice or cauliflower rice, garnished with fresh cilantro.

Storage: This curry keeps well in the refrigerator for up to 5 days and freezes beautifully for up to 3 months.
Meal prep tip: This is one of the best meal prep recipes — make a full batch on Sunday and portion into individual containers for the week. The flavors deepen overnight.
Celiac safety note: Check curry powder labels carefully. Some brands add wheat flour as a filler. Recommended gluten-free curry powders: Simply Organic, Frontier Co-op, or any labeled "certified gluten-free."

---

Practical Guide: Getting Started with Gluten-Free Cooking

For people newly diagnosed with celiac disease, transitioning to a gluten-free kitchen can feel overwhelming. Here are evidence-based tips from our dietitian team:

1. Focus on naturally gluten-free whole foods first: quinoa, rice, potatoes, sweet potatoes, legumes, fresh vegetables, fruits, lean meats, fish, eggs, nuts, and seeds. These foods are inherently safe and highly nutritious.

2. Stock your pantry with these celiac-safe staples: certified gluten-free oats (Bob's Red Mill tests to <10 ppm), quinoa, brown rice, chickpea flour, almond flour, tamari (gluten-free soy sauce), coconut aminos, and certified gluten-free spice blends.

3. Prevent cross-contamination: Use separate cutting boards, toasters, and colanders for gluten-free cooking. According to the Celiac Disease Foundation, even 10 milligrams of gluten (roughly 1/8 teaspoon of flour) can cause intestinal damage in people with celiac disease.

4. Read every label, every time: Ingredients can change without notice. Look for "certified gluten-free" seals from GFCO (Gluten-Free Certification Organization), which guarantees products test below 10 ppm gluten — stricter than the FDA's 20 ppm threshold.

5. Nutritional completeness matters: A common concern is that gluten-free diets may lack B vitamins and iron (typically fortified in wheat products). Our recipes emphasize ingredients that naturally provide these nutrients: spinach (iron, folate), quinoa (B vitamins, iron, magnesium), chickpeas (folate, iron, zinc), and sweet potatoes (vitamin A, vitamin C, potassium).

More recipes and detailed guides available at: https://nutreeliya.com

Here are celiac-friendly dinner ideas that keep the same “regular” flavors by using gluten-free pasta, tortillas, thickeners, and mixes. Each item links to proven gluten-free versions or clear approaches.

Comfort-food classics (GF versions that taste like the originals)
- Gluten-Free Enchiladas (Chicken, red sauce) – use certified GF corn tortillas and enchilada sauce; great weeknight staple [Source 7].
- Easy Gluten-Free Lasagna – swap in gluten-free lasagna noodles; rich and familiar flavors [Source 7].
- The Best Sloppy Joes – same saucy comfort, served on GF buns [Source 7].
- Gluten-Free Alfredo Sauce with GF fettuccine – creamy, classic alfredo that’s naturally GF when thickened properly; pair with GF pasta [Source 7].
- Gluten-Free Chicken Pot Pie (with easy biscuit topping) – all the cozy flavors using GF biscuit topping/flour blends [Source 7].
- BEST Gluten-Free Shepherd’s Pie – naturally GF mash on top with a savory filling (ensure thickeners/sauces are GF) [Source 7].
- Easy, Gluten-Free Mac and Cheese – use your favorite GF macaroni for an indistinguishable “regular” taste/texture when cooked al dente [Source 7].

Family-friendly one-pan hits (fast, crowd-pleasing)
- Cheesy Salsa Verde Chicken and Rice – one-pan, 20-minute dinner with “regular” Tex-Mex flavors (all ingredients are naturally GF when you choose GF salsa/stock) [Source 9].
- Black Bean & Sweet Potato Chicken Enchilada Skillet – big enchilada flavors in one skillet; use GF enchilada sauce [Source 9].
- Mushroom, Spinach & Sun-Dried Tomato Cheesy Chicken Skillet – creamy, cheesy skillet that tastes like your usual weeknight favorite, done gluten-free [Source 9].

Make “old go-tos” gluten-free with smart swaps
- Tamale Pie – use a store-bought gluten-free cornbread mix for the topping to recreate the classic without gluten [Source 2].

Tips to keep taste and texture close to “regular”
- Choose quality GF stand-ins: good GF pasta (cook just to al dente), certified GF tortillas, and reliable GF flour blends. Different flour mixes can yield different results—follow recipe notes and be ready to tweak liquid or bake time slightly [Source 4].
- Always verify every ingredient is gluten-free (broths, sauces, spice blends, tortillas, pasta). Ingredient lists and formulations can change; check labels every time [Source 4].
- Prevent cross-contact (separate toaster, cutting boards, colanders) so flavors shine without risk of gluten exposure [Source 4].

Sources: Meaningful Eats’ Top 25 Gluten-Free Dinner Recipes (classic comfort dishes in GF form) [Source 7]; Iowa Girl Eats’ One-Pan Gluten-Free Recipes (fast, family-friendly meals) [Source 9]; Delish’s celiac-friendly dinner approach (turning old go-tos, like tamale pie, gluten-free with convenient mixes) [Source 2]; National Celiac Association recipe hub and baking/safety notes [Source 4].
